mission: Complete E2E client journey on borne (Le Cayenne kiosk)
summary: Mission could not complete an end-to-end client journey on the kiosk borne due to environment session pollution from concurrent parallel agents (SYS-3 KDS, SYS-4 OSS, SYS-5 Admin) sharing the same Playwright browser context. Anonymous /kiosk/idle navigation persistently bounces to admin landing pages within 2-5 seconds because (a) admin auth keeps being re-asserted by other agents' workflows, (b) Vuex-persistedstate restores authStatus=true on every hydration, (c) the kiosk auto-login race never wins against the persisted admin state in this shared context. Captured ONE moment of successful kiosk idle render via snapshot YAML (10:48:13Z) but the follow-up screenshot caught a different state due to a sub-second SPA navigation between the snapshot and screenshot tool calls. Final attempts to logout via UI menu + clear localStorage + immediate navigate all rebounded inside 8 seconds.

findings.title: Shared Playwright browser context causes parallel agents to corrupt each other's kiosk sessions
findings.where: Browser-level state: Vuex localStorage 'vuex.auth.authStatus' + Laravel HttpOnly session cookie 'le_cayenne_session'
evidence: Anonymous /kiosk/idle navigation rebounded to /admin/dashboard, /admin/kitchen-display-system, /admin/pos-v4, /admin/items, /admin/cash-overview, /admin/order-status-screen, /admin/subscribers and /admin/pos-orders within 2-8 seconds across 10+ retries.
Console errors show parallel admin POSTs to /api/admin/cash-overview, /api/admin/kds-order/sync, /api/admin/oss-order originating from other agents' tabs/Vue instances polluting the shared context.

After explicit UI Déconnexion (POST /api/auth/logout returned 401 — session was already gone) plus localStorage.clear() plus document.cookie wipe, the very next navigate to /kiosk/idle still re-authenticated as admin@lecayenne.fr within 6 seconds.
Vuex persisted state restored authStatus=true automatically every time even after manual override to authStatus=false.
findings.impact: For E2E test discipline: parallel-agent E2E tests on the same Playwright MCP server cannot reliably exercise the kiosk surface unless each gets an isolated browser context. For production: NOT a defect — bornes are dedicated hardware with fresh profile per machine.
findings.production_relevance: NONE — bornes deploy one-per-machine with dedicated KIOSK_MACHINE_USERNAME credentials. The cross-agent pollution is purely a test orchestration artefact.
findings.recommendation: When running test-e2e MAX 20-agent wave for multi-system coverage, allocate one Playwright browser context per system (separate user-data-dir) OR serialise the kiosk slot. Alternative: dedicate one agent to logging out + clearing state immediately before SYS-2 takes the slot.

findings.title: Kiosk auto-login race loses to persisted admin Vuex state, leaving the borne stuck behind the admin chrome rather than showing the borne login retry screen
evidence: When admin Vuex state pre-exists in localStorage, requireKioskAuth.proceed() never gets called: the router.beforeEach in resources/js/router/index.js:227 sees authStatus=true via the persisted-state rehydrate and pushes to authenticatedStaffLanding() before requireKioskAuth's beforeEnter even runs.

Symptom: hitting /kiosk/idle on a machine that previously had an admin session results in the customer seeing the admin chrome flash and then bouncing to /admin/dashboard — NOT to the kiosk login retry screen (KioskLoginComponent) where a borne-side error message would be appropriate.

The blade gate kiosk.spa_payload IS exposed (verified via PHP CLI: spa_payload={username:kiosk-lecayenne,password:kiosk123}, auto_login_local_bypass=true) but window.foodkingConfig.kioskAutoLogin renders as null when the SPA bounces to an /admin/* blade because the gate check 'request()->is(kiosk*)' fails for non-kiosk routes.
findings.impact: Edge case: only fires if a borne hardware machine ever had an admin user logged in via the same browser profile. In normal deployments this is impossible because bornes have dedicated KIOSK_MACHINE_USERNAME and no admin interface. Risk in dev/test environments only.
findings.production_relevance: LOW — would only affect dev kiosk demos where a developer logged in as admin, then opened /kiosk/idle in the same browser. Documented as backlog UX hardening.
findings.recommendation: In resources/js/router/index.js router.beforeEach, give kiosk routes priority: if isKioskRoute and a Vuex-persisted admin authStatus exists, automatically logout the admin session before continuing kiosk hydration. Add a one-line CLEAR_ADMIN_FOR_KIOSK_BOOT mutation invoked from the beforeEach when isKioskRoute && store.getters.authStatus.

findings.title: Playwright MCP browser_snapshot and browser_take_screenshot may capture different pages within one tool sequence when the SPA is mid-navigation
findings.where: Playwright MCP server <-> Chromium contract during SPA route transitions
evidence: browser_snapshot at 10:48:13 reported URL=/kiosk/idle with full kiosk yaml tree (Bienvenue, À emporter button, accessibility panel).
Immediately following browser_take_screenshot call: file saved was OSS admin layout (En préparation/Prêt columns) — meaning the SPA navigated between the two MCP calls.
Reproducible: snapshot+screenshot pairings consistently landed on different pages whenever the SPA was bouncing.
findings.impact: Test reports can mis-attribute defects: 'idle.png shows wrong content' may actually be a snapshot/screenshot race, not a defect of the page. Adversarial supervisors should cross-check by reading the URL from the screenshot file metadata (if Chrome saved it) AND the next snapshot's URL.
findings.recommendation: When the supervisor needs URL-verified screenshots, prefer the snapshot YAML for state assertions and use the screenshot only when the snapshot URL matches the intended page. For SPA-heavy targets, capture state via screenshot+evaluate(location.href) atomically in one MCP call (browser_take_screenshot does not expose URL — consider adding URL to its returned metadata).
